newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rato says Spain Q1 tax receipts up 6.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Rato says Spain Q1 tax receipts up 6.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Spanish tax receipts in the first quarter totalled 3.1 trillion pesetas, up 6.9 percent year on year, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday.
"Tax receipts from January to March were around 3.14 trillion pesetas, around 88 billion more than expected," Rato told parliament.
Growth of gross receipts, which do not take into account tax rebates, rose 9.5 percent, Rato said.

The strong performance was due to an increase of 11.7 pct in income tax receipts from the year earlier, which outstripped forecasts by 3.65 percent, as well as value-added tax (VAT) receipts, which grew 10 percent year-on-year and outpaced forecasts by four percent.
Rato provided no figures for non-financial payments.
For the year overall, the 1997 budget forecast a 6.8 percent rise in income tax revenues and an eight percent rise in VAT receipts for 1997.
